title: Model loading & weight management - draft spec
summary: Draft design for model weight loading and memory management in the serving runtime. Covers lazy load, mmap-backed storage, safetensors I/O, hot-swap semantics, eviction/prefetch heuristics, and integration with the request scheduler and KV cache.
background: As we support larger open models and multi-tenant Dedicated clusters, we need predictable memory usage, low tail latency, and flexible weight deployment. Current runtime eagerly loads full model weights into GPU memory which increases cold-start times and reduces multiplexing efficiency. This spec proposes a layered approach (lazy load + mmap + safetensors + hot-swap) to reduce memory footprint and improve throughput while preserving inference correctness and safety.
goals: 1) Reduce cold-start latency for infrequently used models and model variants. 2) Increase effective GPU utilization by enabling on-demand weight residency. 3) Support atomic model updates (hot-swap) with zero-downtime routing for in-flight requests. 4) Maintain compatibility with safetensors and standard PyTorch/ONNX checkpoints. 5) Provide clear metrics and rollout plan for safe deployment.
constraints: - Must not violate request-level consistency guarantees. - Minimal change to public serving API. - Prioritize correctness and stability over aggressive optimizations for initial rollout. - Work across cloud VMs with local NVMe, NFS-mounted stores, and object store-backed staging. - Support quantized and unquantized weight formats.
design_overview: We introduce a weight management layer between model artifact storage and the runtime executor. Key components: (A) on-disk canonical representation (prefer safetensors + index metadata), (B) mmap-backed read-only region for CPU-side tensors, (C) on-demand GPU staging path with async DMA and kernel-friendly layout, (D) a residency manager (LRU + priority pins) that reacts to scheduler hints and KV cache accesses, and (E) an atomic hot-swap path that stages a new version and flips routes when safe.
lazy_load_strategy: - Default behavior: do not eagerly upload all tensors to GPU. - Maintain a lightweight model descriptor with per-tensor residency state (resident_on: cpu|gpu|mmapped|remote). - On first access to a tensor during execution, schedule an async staging job to transfer the tensor to GPU. If the tensor is required synchronously for the first micro-batch, we employ a fast path that blocks the worker thread up to a configurable timeout before falling back to a slower path (smaller micro-batch or CPU fallback). - Allow configuration overrides per-model: eager (legacy), hybrid (embeddings & attention keys prefetched), lazy (default).
mmap_and_disk_layout: - Store canonical tensors as safetensors on disk with an accompanying index file describing byte offsets, dtype, shape, sharding info, and preferred device layout. - Expose optional memory-mapped read-only regions for CPU-side tensors (mmap) to avoid double-copy when reading weights for CPU fallback or quantization. - For NVMe-local stores we prefer mmap with advice MADV_SEQUENTIAL for initial startup, and MADV_WILLNEED for prefetch heuristics. - For network filesystems or object stores, a local staging area (shared with other processes) caches safetensors and builds mmapped views. - Ensure page alignment and consistent endianness; include small versioned header in the index for compatibility checks.
safetensors_support: - Primary on-disk format: safetensors because of speed, deterministic layout, and safe parsing. - Loader will validate magic + index checksum before exposing tensors. - Provide conversion tooling in runtime to accept legacy .pt/.bin artifacts as a pre-deploy step (CI job). - Metadata fields: model_version, build_id, layer_names, tensor_offsets, dtype, quantization_info, contiguous_layout_hint. - For quantized tensors, include dequant metadata and optional fused-layout descriptors to match kernel expectations.
hot_swap_mechanism: - Hot-swap is atomic from the router's perspective: new version is staged (download -> validate -> mmap -> warm prefetch) on a disjoint residency namespace. - During staging, in-flight requests continue against the previous version. - After sanity checks and optional canary traffic, perform an atomic routing flip by updating a lightweight model pointer in the control-plane (atomic CAS). - Residency manager continues to evict old-version tensors based on policy; we do not force immediate eviction to avoid thrash. - Expose a TTL grace window to allow long-lived sessions to drain before forced eviction. - Edge conditions: if new version fails validation, rollback and emit incident metrics.
weight_eviction_and_prefetch: - Residency manager uses a multi-tier policy: pinned tensors (embeddings + output heads), high-priority prefetch list (attention keys for low-latency configs), and LRU buckets. - Scheduler provides access hints (next N tokens, expected sequence lengths) to inform prefetch. - Eviction respects pinned weights and model-shared tensors across variants. - Prefetch heuristics: prefetch first-layer weights for batched requests, attention KV matrices for large batch sizes, and decoder weights for autoregressive workloads. - Allow operator policies: aggressive eviction (High multiplexing), conservative (low thrash), leak-resident for performance debugging.
integration_with_scheduler_and_kv_cache: - Scheduler exposes predicted call patterns (e.g., chat sessions vs stateless generations) and a weight_hint API: weight_hint(model, tensor_list, priority, deadline_ms). - KV cache accesses route through residency manager; hot KV entries can pin corresponding attention weights temporarily. - On response streaming, scheduler can request prioritized staging of next-step keys to reduce token latency. - If a tensor is not resident in GPU and the scheduler indicates a strict latency SLO, runtime can either block briefly to stage or return a graceful degradation token (e.g., CPU fallback or return partial stream) depending on model policy.
rollout_and_migration_plan: Phase 0: internal canaries on dev clusters - small models with synthetic traffic, compare latency and correctness vs eager baseline. Phase 1: opt-in beta for select customers and engine teams, hybrid mode where critical tensors are pinned. Phase 2: default lazy mode for non-critical models, provide toggle in Console. Phase 3: enable hot-swap workflows for Dedicated customers with explicit SLA guardrails. Each phase requires bench jobs, fallout mitigation playbooks, and canary thresholds (95p token latency increase < 10ms, accuracy regressions < predefined eval delta).
metrics_and_benchmarks: Track: cold-start time (time from route to first token), per-tensor stage latency, cache miss rate (tensor-level), eviction churn, additional p50/p95/p99 token latency delta vs baseline, GPU memory utilization, network I/O for staging, successful hot-swap rate, rollback incidence. Baseline targets: cold-start reduced by >=40% for large models, cache miss rate <15% under steady workloads for configured warm models.
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for loader/validator (safetensors checksum, index correctness). - Integration tests for mmap path on NVMe and NFS. - Fuzz tests for partial file corruption and graceful failures. - Load tests with synthetic and recorded production traces to validate eviction heuristics. - Chaos tests around hot-swap during heavy load (force version fail during flip). - A/B with production workloads comparing throughput & tail latency.
security_considerations: - Validate safetensors headers and disallow arbitrary Python deserialization pipelines. - Enforce artifact signing and verify signatures before staging. - Limit mmap exposure to unprivileged process pages; clear mmap mappings before removing artifacts to avoid stale-memory leaks. - Ensure hot-swap cannot be abused to escalate: route changes must be authorized and audited, and an operator can exclusively pin versions for compliance.
operational_playbook: - Alerts: high eviction churn, staging queue backlog, increased cold-starts, hot-swap rollbacks. - Runbook steps: toggle model to eager mode, increase prefetch budget, scale capacity, or rollback model version. - Provide diagnostic endpoints: residency snapshot, per-tensor residency timestamps, last-stage error. - Metrics emitted to Console and supportable via Alerts and traces.
open_questions: 1) Best default prefetch list for decoder-only vs encoder-decoder models? 2) How to version index format without breaking older agents? 3) Should we support transparent on-the-fly quantization during staging? 4) Policy for multi-tenant GPU when two models compete for pinned tensors? 5) Runtime memory leak detection for mmapped files across forks/process restarts?
